page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.large is a memory-optimized instance based on the AWS Nitro System, engineered for workloads requiring a high memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside low-latency local storage. It is powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 2 dedicated vCPUs across 1 physical core with multithreading enabled. The instance is provisioned with 16 GB of DDR4 system memory operating at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU allocation, and includes a bundled 75 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume. Baseline network performance is rated at 2 Gbps, and no GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest multi-threaded compute capabilities alongside typical single-core performance. The server achieved a single-core Geekbench score of 1190.0, aligning with midrange expectations, while its multi-core result of 1430.0 reflects the limits of its single physical core design. Memory bandwidth reached 13.51 GB/sec read and 11.59 GB/sec write on 256 MB uncached blocks, with cached small-block reads measuring 96.32 GB/sec. Application testing yielded 1.52 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.55 GB/sec static web throughput, confirming moderate I/O and processing boundaries.

The hardware configuration provides high memory density and high-speed temporary storage relative to its core count, making it a viable option for deployments limited more by memory and disk latency than compute overhead. Tradeoffs include modest parallel compute capacity and lower network baseline rates. The instance is suited for small in-memory key-value stores, intermediate data transformation pipelines, local scratch processing, and development or staging database environments.
